*** Add File: /mnt/c/Users/cabot/OneDrive/Documents/Research/Cambridge/X3I/mhd_llm/codex/observations/athena_ct_export/README.md
+# Isolated Athena CT ecliptic output helper
+
+Ready header: `solver/athena_ct/ecliptic_export.hpp`. This header has no solver dependency and does not allocate or copy a 3D field volume. It has not been wired into the Athena generator or core.
+
+```cpp
+#include "ecliptic_export.hpp"
+using athena_ct_export::EclipticExport;
+using athena_ct_export::Fields;
+
+EclipticExport movie(out, radii, thetas, phis,
+    std::filesystem::path("inputs/ecliptic_to_solar_matrix.csv"),
+    512, 2.3, "2025-11-01T00:00:00Z");
+
+// Call only after accepting a step. Preserve the solver's untrimmed timestep.
+movie.write(actual_day, [&](int i, int j, int k) -> Fields {
+    return physical_cell_fields(i, j, k);
+});
+```
+
+The accessor returns `[n, vr, vtheta, vphi, p, Br, Btheta, Bphi]` in `cm^-3`, `km/s`, `nPa`, and `nT`, at the actual cell centers. It is read only. Only density and velocity are used. Axes are increasing `std::vector<double>`: radius in AU, colatitude in radians strictly between the poles, and a full-period longitude axis in radians without a duplicated endpoint. Any common longitude phase is accepted. Ghost cells must not be included as physical axes unless their values are intentionally part of the sampling domain.
+
+The inline-basis constructor replaces the CSV argument with `std::array<double,9> matrix, std::string matrix_source`. Matrix rows map ecliptic Cartesian coordinates to the solver's Cartesian coordinates. The helper checks a finite proper rotation and writes the exact numbers and source to metadata. The default pixel count is 512; 2 through 768 are allowed. Passing zero makes construction/writes perform no I/O or accessor calls, including no CSV read. There is no solver state, timestep, source, or floor change.
+
+The constructor caches each in-domain pixel's eight corner indices/weights and spherical basis vectors. `write(day, accessor)` reconstructs Cartesian number momentum `n*v` at those corners, interpolates it, and writes `|interpolated(n*v)|*1e5`. This equals the interpolated density times the magnitude of interpolated conserved velocity. It is heliocentric bulk proton flux, not comet-relative incident flux. Pressure and magnetic fields are not interpolated for this product.
+
+Output uses the existing movie-reader interface:
+
+- `ecliptic_x_au.npy`, `ecliptic_y_au.npy`: increasing float32 coordinates, endpoints ±2.3 AU by default. These stored coordinates define the sampled positions.
+- `ecliptic_flux_00000.npy`, etc.: float32 `[y,x]` flux in `cm^-2 s^-1`. NaN marks the central hole, radial exterior, and latitude exterior beyond the interpolable cell-center domain. Longitude interpolation is periodic, including the seam.
+- `snapshots.csv`: `day,file`, with the caller's actual accepted epoch written to 17 significant digits. Days must be finite and strictly increasing. No temporal interpolation or timestep clipping is performed.
+- `ecliptic_slice_metadata.json`: plane, extent, coordinates, units, interpolation, basis and domain provenance, origin UTC, cache size and valid-pixel count.
+
+The helper must be the sole writer of its plane directory's main `snapshots.csv`; a manifest with existing data rows is rejected. It intentionally does not implement resume, sparse 3D output, full-state snapshots, or main-case metadata/probe writing. The caller can keep its existing separate sparse diagnostic exporter. A bad accessor sample throws before any frame or manifest row is written.
+
+Qualification: `python observations/athena_ct_export/run_tests.py` compiles and executes one isolated C++ fixture, then independently reconstructs conserved Cartesian momentum from the saved eight physical fields and checks every pixel with SciPy `RegularGridInterpolator`. The script uses one CPU and caps scientific-library threads. It recreates only its own `fixtures/` directory.
+
+`verification.json` records 32 C++ checks and eight field/grid/basis cases. Maximum relative discrepancy against SciPy is `5.783e-8`; masks agree exactly. Tests cover constant Cartesian momentum with varying density, radial analytic refinement, nonconstant periodic fields, seam sampling, identity and exact production rotation, narrow rotated latitude mask, actual epoch preservation, CSV/inline byte identity, default-off no I/O, and invalid-input rejection. The radial field's analytic interpolation error decreases by 3.962 on doubling the angular resolution. The production-sized 512² cache is 53,500,864 bytes; fixture peak RSS is 57,400 KiB. Conservative summed Python/compiler peak bound is 263,644 KiB. Compilation has no warnings.
+
+These gates qualify the isolated exporter only. After integration, Athena caller identity must still be checked with output disabled versus enabled at untrimmed accepted steps; this work makes no claim about CT solver accuracy, stability, convergence, or scientific validation.
